newsitem.title: USA: Progress called limited on U.S., Japan trade rows.
newsitem.headline: Progress called limited on U.S., Japan trade rows.

text.p: The United States and Japan have made enough progress on port access talks to defer U.S. sanctions until September but movement on civil aviation talks has been much more limited, the State Department said on Monday.

"These are two important trade issues with Japan...I cannot report full satisfaction on either of them although more on the ports and less on civil air," department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
Japan and the United States signed a Memorandum of Consultation Friday addressing the major issues discussed during 10 days of talks.

Maritime Administrator Albert Herberger said Japan agreed to approve applications from U.S. carriers for operations at Japanese ports and to deregulate the licensing system for port transportation business.
On the issue of competition for stevedoring services in Japan, negotiators endorsed an interim agreement providing a framework for reforming the system by July 31, Herberger said.

He gave no details of the plan but Burns said Monday Japanese government officials would consult with authorities who control Japanese ports "to make sure American firms will then have adequate access to compete for contracts." Burns added: "We've essentially kicked the can down the road until Sept. 4, '97" on this issue.
